I'll think this through like the farmer I am — 30 years in these fields, I know what works here.

**My thinking:**

I have 9 mu. Here in Quzhou, most people do wheat-maize double crop — that's how I feed my family of 7. But I also keep some cotton because it brings cash. I'll put 6 mu to wheat-maize and 3 mu to cotton. Cotton takes the whole season, so those 3 mu won't grow wheat after.

For wheat — I plant in October after the maize comes out. I use improved seed, the kind the seed dealer in town sells, "Jimai" type. Last year I put down 2 bags of compound fertilizer (about 50 kg each) before planting, plus a bag of urea at green-up in spring. That's about 20 kg N per mu, 9 kg phosphorus, 6 kg potassium. I water 3 times — once before winter, once at jointing, once when the grain is filling. I got about 500 kg per mu last year so I'll aim for that again. I spray twice — once for aphids, once for the yellow rust if I see it.

For maize — I plant right after wheat harvest in June, no tillage, just drill it in. I use hybrid seed, everyone does now. I put urea on twice — about 18 kg N per mu total, with 5 kg phosphorus and 5 kg potassium mixed in at planting. One irrigation at tasseling if no rain. Spray once for the borer. I expect 550 kg per mu.

For cotton — this one needs more care. I plough the land, plant improved Bt cotton seed so bollworm isn't as bad. Still I spray 5 times against aphids and mites. I put 15 kg N per mu split in two applications, 8 kg phosphorus, 8 kg potassium. Water twice. I hope for 220 kg per mu of seed cotton.

I'd rather use a little extra fertilizer than see my crop hungry. Losing yield is worse than spending some extra money on urea.
